_about: Obadiah Sedgwick (1600?-1658), member of the Westminster Assembly and minister at Covent Garden: The Fountain Opened, sermons on Isaiah 55:1-3 (London, 1657); The Shepherd of Israel, sermons on the whole twenty-third Psalm, with the doctrine of Providence on Matthew 10:29-31 (London, 1658); The Anatomy of Secret Sins (London, 1660); The Humbled Sinner Resolved what he should do to be Saved (London, 1660); and The Bowels of Tender Mercy Sealed in the Everlasting Covenant (London, 1661), the last four published after his death from his corrected notes. The Princeton copies are 17th-century printings scanned from the books; the Bowels is an EEBO scan. Internet Archive OCR, raw and unconverted; each title page read before listing.

sedgwick-anatomy-secret-sins-1660.author: The OCR breaks the name: the title page reads 'By that Reverend and Faithfull Minister of the Gospel Mr. Obadiab Sedgwic^ B. D. ... LONDON, Printed by T. R. for Adoniram Byfield', 1660, the same publisher as the Fountain Opened.

sedgwick-bowels-tender-mercy-1661.author: The OCR breaks the name: the title page reads 'By that Faithful Reverend Divine Mr. Obadiab Sedo[...] B.D. late Minister of the Gospel in Covent-Garden, London', printed for Adoniram Byfield, 1661; the preface opens 'Had not the Reverend Author of this Book requested our Attestation unto all the Pieces which after his death should be printed in his Name'.
